observation_summary: The command-line parser fails to correctly merge default argument values with user-provided arguments. When a user provides fewer arguments than the maximum allowed, the system ignores the remaining default values instead of appending them to the list of provided values.
hypothesis: The logic responsible for populating the command-line argument list (likely in WriteableCommandLineImpl) incorrectly assumes that if any arguments are provided, the default values should be ignored entirely, rather than filling the remaining slots up to the defined maximum or required count.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the method that retrieves or populates argument values to check if the number of provided arguments is less than the maximum allowed, and if so, append the remaining default values to the result list.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly states that the patch 'fixes the default values behavior by adding the missing values to the list'. This confirms the issue is a procedural logic error in how the argument list is constructed when defaults are present.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a procedural error in the argument collection logic. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment), or a design-level capability issue (Function/Class/Object). It is a flaw in the algorithm that determines the final list of arguments by failing to correctly combine user input with default values.
evidence_used: Bug report comments regarding the patch

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not that a variable is initialized to the wrong value, but that the procedure for merging two sets of values (user-provided and defaults) is logically incomplete.
While there is a condition involved (how many arguments are provided), the fix is not just adding a guard, but implementing the logic to correctly aggregate the argument list.
